meta_description_en: Readers' letters in Outlet #30 (February 1990): Sam Coupe first impressions, OPD microdrive conversion, PCG DTP, Datel mouse, and Francis Miles's "Index to the Spectrum ROM".
meta_description_ru: Письма читателей журнала Outlet #30 (февраль 1990): впечатления о Sam Coupe, переделка микродрайвов OPD, DTP от PCG, мышь от Datel и «Index to the Spectrum ROM» Фрэнсиса Майлза.

From Norman Evans, MIDDLESBROUGH

I have recently received the Sam
Coupe computer. It looks like it
will be o.k. for most games but
other software, such as word
processors and databases, will
need a lot of work [to convert
from Spectrum]. It has some nice
touches but certain commands
such as INKEY fail to respond
and I find I have to use the GET
command to replace them. Be
careful with the accidental use
of command words when using
PRINT staements as the line can
be corrupted easily.

Thanks, Norman. Hopefully, the
ROM bugs will be ironed out by
MGT in due course. - Brian

From E.J. Shuker, ILFRACOMBE
Re:E.M. Duffield's conversion of
OPD microdrives(# 14),Miniature
Tool Co. have disappeared but I
have all the necessary items.One
query is on item 3.Is a "dual 8-
way reversing card" just a piece
of fibreglass with 8 tracks
(parallel)each side? If so,I can
go ahead. I plan to leave the
ribbon cable where it is and re-
route the connections.

The one I have has SEVEN tracks
(matching the connector)but each
goes THROUGH a hole in the PCB
and to its opposite contact BUT
ON THE OTHER SIDE.Why? I thought
the top and bottom parts of
these clips were two halfs of
one contact. Anyone know if
direct tracks would do? -Brian

From A. Allen, POOLE

Does anybody know if P.C.G.'s
DTP package is any good or if
Datel Electronics mouse system
works on the +3 and what other
software it works on?


P.C.G.'s DTP suite is generally
highly-rated but I and some
others think the average user
would need to study it for quite
some time to really get the hang
of it.It does not work correctly
with my early Interface 1 so do
not use it myself. For a review
see OUTLET 8 and 16.

Does anyone know about the Datel
Mouse?
            - Brian

From:- Malcolm Goodman, WELWYN

Judging from the number of
enquiries I had when my 'books
for sale' advert appeared, there
are still a few people who would
like to get their hands on the
Logan/O'Hara ROM disassembly.
Although this is now out of
print, I received some sample
pages from'Index to the Spectrum
ROM' written by Francis G. Miles
(author of'Word Manager').F.G.M.
has taken the ROM disassembly a
stage further and has virtually
dissected the Spectrum,resulting
in an extended study of every
subroutine,system variable,flag,
BASIC command and function, key
code and operating system of the
48k Spectrum. This has been done
in the form of an index.

Those who own Logan will find
this supplements the book whilst
those who don't should still
derive great use from the study.

There are some sample pages and
introduction available on
request giving an indication of
the enormous amount of work that
has gone into producing this
index which runs to about 450
single-sided pages.Alternatively
the index can be supplied on 5 x
5.25 discs with the Word Manager
word processor to print it out.

If any outleteer is interested
they should send an s.a.e.(fool-
scap size) to:- Francis G. Miles
'Windrush' Rabley Heath, Welwyn,
Herts AL6 9UF

I've discovered you can page in
a +D from BASIC with RANDOMIZE
USR 102 - irrespective of the
contents at 23728/9. In fact any
USR from 94 - 102 will page in
the +D, allowing the snapshot
opion. USR 93 is a "funny". USR
132 also seems to page the +D.

Quite frankly, I don't know why,
as it's not something that
fails standard Speccy syntax.
Perhaps someone who knows the +D
well, can explain.

Now to something I've either
forgotten or never knew. Where
does the Spectrum get its
GRAPHIC shapes (CHR$ 128 - 143)
from? Where in ROM are they
held?

To Malcolm Goodman from Brian
Thanks, Malcolm.The index sounds
like an excellent reference work
and I'm surprised it's not more
well known. I wonder what sort
of price he is asking for the
set of discs? If he's producing
it professionally for software
houses it could be quite pricey
but if he's just making a token
charge or even letting it go as
public domain perhaps he might
let us serialize it in OUTLET?!!

The graphic shapes aren't stored
as bit-patterns like a char set
but formed from algorithms at
0B38 to 0B51, to save space. In
BONABANNER, I made a bit-pattern
copy so I could use SCREEN$ to
transfer images to BASIC string
graphics.             - Brian

From Carlo Vireca, MILAN

I own a Disciple but I am not
able to get SAVE and LOAD on
disk making use of machine code.
Can you help please?

We've never explored that area
because programs using machine
code to access the drives become
incompatible with other systems.
It is usually best to return to
BASIC which can be easily modif-
ied by the user. However,I think
you want this purely to modify
your OCP assembler which only
SAVEs to tape. If you have found
the tape routines in the OCP
code, you might try to force a
return to BASIC to access the
drives. Can anyone else help?
                      - Brian

From: Anthony J. Perrin, N.10

Reference the letter from R.C.
Armstrong (OUTLET 28) - fit a
"push-to-make" pushbutton switch
with flying leads coming outside
of the keyboard casing to
connect contact strips 6B or 7B
with 20b on the underside of the
edge-connector (0 volts - reset)
to make a reset switch. A light
touch with a soldering iron is
quite O.K. and there is enough
room behind the actual contact
area to tack on a wire.It worked
for me!(Source: Spectrum Harware
Manual by Adrian Dickens).



Many thanks, Anthony     - Brian

From Mike Haine, LEAMINGTON SPA

Hi Bron! (Brian + Ron! See?)

The more I see of OUTLET and
these letters in particular the
more I like it! It compares esp-
ecially favourably with FORMAT,
which has a miserable letters
section.

Re. query on the RESET Button. I
made this change several years
ago and still have instructions.
The reset button is a normally
open push button, readily avail-
able from Tandy's (for example).
It is connected across the cond-
ensor labelled C27 on the PCB.
This component is in different
places on the different Spectrum
issues as shown in a diagram.

Will lend instructions to anyone
writing. [Mike's address is in
OUTBOARD - B.C.]

Re THE PRINTER CLUB; I have had
had a fair response to this, and
have sent out a questionnaire in
an attempt to gather info on
individuals' set ups etc. Only
about 5 of these have been
returned to date. I have been
able to sort out a few problems
and put one or two parties in
contact with others with same or
similar set ups. I'd like to get
more details like this so that I
can put them all together and
issue a summary. One or two of
you have generously lent me
instruction books from which I
have been able to photocopy the


important pages to send to
others who have, for example,
printers without books. I have
also sent out some introductory
notes and a little memo suggest-
ing how you can explore the
capabilities of your printer.
I'll send a copy to the mag. as
it may be of interest.

I'd like to contact any who are
regularly using Tasword 2 and
who would be willing to try out
some more mods I have made!

Re Scott Brown's remarks on
Carol Brooksbank; after seeing
this I phoned Carol. She doesn't
take OUTLET and I read the
comments to her. She says she is
fully occupied with her progs
for Format and other activities.

Perhaps you(Bron) might interest
her if you sent a sample copy
but I got the impression she
would not undertake any more
commitments. Her address is in
the Coventry directory.

           Mike Haine.

Thanks Mike although it doesn't
sound very promising does it?

Thanks for the comments in your
other letter to me about extend-
ing our distribution which we'll
keep in mind. However, as ever,
both Ron and I are pushed to the
limit with the present workload
and now SAM.....

                - Brian

From Ian Wooff, BELMONT




Dear Ron/Brian,

Which,if any, joystick interface
will work with the +D?




I have never heard of any joy-
stick interface clashing with
the +D. Can any readers with +Ds
working with a joystick please
write in and tell us?

                     - Brian

From P.M. Scrivener, MALDON



Does anyone know the name and
address of a supplier of a midi
lead for the +3?






I have been unable to find any
advertisements for these leads.
Possibly they are a standard
cable which can be bought in
musical instrument shops? Anyone
know?

                     - Brian

From Les Tyler, CHELTENHAM.

I may have uncovered a bug in
the tape version of SHELLSHOCK,
which I'd like you to chase up,
if you would. Using my header
reader, the code section appears
to be 36656 bytes long, starting
at 28860, whereas the note in
the BASIC portion indicates a
start address of 28865 and a
code length of 36671. Perhaps my
arithmetic is a bit shaky, but
something tells me there is a
bit of a *-*/-up here somewhere!
Suffice it to say that I can't
transfer a working copy to disc
as yet!

COL80+ is splendid for my purp-
oses;I get through text files in

very little time at all. One
thing I notice in your replies
to letters is that the program
prints various single letters
prior to an answer, e.g. (c...
rubbish...)(e..I agree...), etc.
Not exactly earth-shaking, but
intriguing. Care to explain?

Any chance of another Ron offer-
ing on the lines of the black
boxes, way back in issue 8? Must
be my warped sense of humour, I
reckon, but I thought it was
marvellous, wish I had thought
of it myself! Cheers! - Les

To Les Tyler from Brian

The correct SHELLSHOCK code is
28860,36656. Did you alter line
9790 to load code from disc?

Odd letters printed by COL80 are
probably codes 26 and the INK
colour, I use if my answer is on
the same page as a writer. I can
think of no easy solution that
would not also be slow! E.g.,you
could load the code separately,
PEEK through and POKE spaces in
any address holding such codes
then reSAVE a temporary copy...

For the past two years, Ron has
been working on an article he's
called "Why I Can't Find Time to
Write Articles" - but that is as
far as he has got.     - Brian

From Neil Morgan, BOLTON


I have been looking into the
Clearcut problem on the Spectrum
+3[move RAMTOP without a CLS-BC]
I agree with you that it should
be simple enough. Amstrad
supposedly left the 48k ROM
pretty well intact but they have
made quite a few subtle but
major changes to it.

I examined the stacks using the
same addresses and similar
disassemblers on a 48k machine
and on the +3 and found that
there were differences in the
return addresses for both errors
and for correctly executed BASIC
lines.

         48k       +3

error   1303      5b3a
ok      1b76      1031

It would appear a simple change
of these values would produce
the desired effect.Unfortunately
the "ok" value on the +3 sends
control to somewhere in the
"editing?" area.

I used the Hisoft monitor to
alter the error vector and
inserted a breakpoint at the new
address. The 48k ROM i.e. ROM 3
was in use at the instant that
control was returned to the
monitor. I have tried the same
thing with the "ok" return value
but the program never reaches

the breakpoint. On further
inspection I found the value on
the stack had been reset to it's
original value. I suspect that
the problem is that a different
ROM is in place when a return is
made using 1031h but I have been
unable to prove this.

Of course it could be that more
values on the stack are used on
the +3 than used to be used on
the 48k, I wish I knew for
certain! Perhaps someone can
shed some more light on this?

Yes please give us plenty of
clip art. I require a picture of
a pedal car!Yes I know it sounds
silly but it is a real sport
with cars costing up to about
`1000 (1 thousand, not a

misprint!) which can travel at
speeds up to about 40 m.p.h.Many
races are 24 hour ones. I need a
picture for a newsletter but I
am not very artistic.

I'm not sure which issue it is
in but Brian Gaff had a routine
in popular computing weekly
about paging between modes on a
+3 which works on some but
requires an initial "SPECTRUM"
mode change on those with bugged
ROMs. I too had difficulty using
tape on a +3. The problem was
easily solved on my machine with
2 custom made leads. The problem
was not with LOADing but the
original SAVE. It seemed to save
but was actually distorted. A
little detective work is needed.

   1. Can any commercial program
be loaded from cassette at all?
If YES then the cassette lead is
ok and the head is probably in
adjustment. If NO then check the
lead is wired correctly bearing
in mind that a stereo plug
should be used at the Spectrum
end.If you still can't load then
check the head alignment.
   2. If you can load some
commercial games but some seem
to load then crash, it may be a
compatibility problem so:- reset
the Spectrum. Go to 48k BASIC
FROM THE MENU. LOAD from tape.
   3.If all(or most)of the above
works then try saving a simple
BASIC program to tape. Listen to
the tape and if it sounds
reasonable try to reload paying
close attention to the volume.

   4.If 1 and 2 work but 3 fails
you will need a specially
modified cassette lead or a
different cassette recorder. If
there is reasonable interest in
the custom leads I shall arrange
for a batch to be made up.

When a disk is sent through the
post it may not always load
straight away. Just like video
and cassette tapes it should be
allowed to reach normal room
temperature and humidity before
any attempt is made to use it. I
tried to load a recent 3" disk
version of OUTLET as soon as it
arrived and it showed several
sector errors. The next day I
loaded and transferred all the
files without problem.

Any chance of the assembler
listing for TANDUM? I have a
friend with a Tandy Lineprinter
VIII which this code almost
works for but the linefeed pitch
seems to be wrong. I have the
manual but cannot quite work out
which bytes to alter to make it
work.
          - Neil Morgan

To Neil Morgan from Brian

Many thanks for all those tips.
There is some very useful info
there. I've not yet had time to
study the CLEARCUT problem again
on the +3. It's one of those
niggling little things that
ought to be dead easy!

Regarding TANDUM I can only say
that I think the codes should
probably be inserted before the
USR call at line 9795 but I'm
sure you already found that out.
As for the source itself I can
only appeal to Arnold Woodruff
or have you any ideas, Arnold?

Can you,or anyone,send photos or
sketches of pedal cars and I'll
do a screen for you - Brian

From: G.L.R. Till, CUMBRIA


Dear Brian,

In reply to your inquiry, print
heads for the M1009 may be
obtained from:

         JONES & BROTHER
      JONES SEWING MACHINE
          COMPANY LTD.
    SHEPLEY STREET, AUDENSHAW
       MANCHESTER, M34 5JD

Prod.Code 01343  1009 Print Head

          Price `19.75

This is better than a 1109 head
which is `31.00!

With regard to your suggestion
about accessing text files for
the WRITER (from Opus), namely
RANDOMIZE USR 4007,unfortunately
it causes a crash.

                 - G.L.R. Till



That's why I think all programs
should access tape or drives
from BASIC so they can be easily
made to work on any system. Has
anyone else done the conversion?

I'm very grateful for the name
and address of a supplier of
M1009 print heads. I shall order
one as soon as I am able.

                       - Brian

From: N.J.D. Whittle, CARLUKE


Dear Sirs,

I have been unable to print out
any of the OUTLET pages. I use a
+3 and a Brother M1509 with its
serial socket connected to the
RS232 socket on the +3.

Using Toni Baker's book "Master-
ing Machine Code on Your
Spectrum", I am learning machine
code. Printing to the screen is
fully described but I would like
to incorporate routines to
output data to my printer. Can
you offer any suggestions?.

To Mr. N.J.D. Whittle from Brian

It has proved impractical to
cover all variations of printer
interface unfortunately but you
can amend it yourself thus...

Select +3 BASIC and enter MERGE
"CONTENTS". Wait for the o.k.
message. Enter LIST 1356. Wait
for the lines to be listed and
then press BREAK twice.Press the
left-pointing arrow key and the
flashing square will move up to
the end of line 1300. Press the
right arrow key until it moves
back down to the space just past
the number 1356 at the start of
the line. Type a space then:
FORMAT LPRINT "R": and ENTER.You
will notice the line already has
a FORMAT LPRINT "U" which will

be pushed along ahead of your
typing. If you get an error BEEP
and the flashing square goes red
then check your typing. Did you
put the colon at the end?

The flashing square should be in
the space below line 1356, above
1364. Type RUN 9970 and ENTER
which will reSAVE the program to
the disc. Re-LOAD OUTLET and try
it.I regret that I have not been
able to test it as I do not have
an RS232 cable but there should
be no problem.

The above instruction highlights
how awful the 128K editor is to
use! If I sounded too pedantic
that's for the sake of any other
readers who do no programming!

To print from machine code try:

       LD A,3      ;stream 3
                   ;= LPRINT
       CALL 5633   ;(1601 hex)
                   ;OPEN CHANNEL
       LD DE,STRING
       LD BC,LENGTH;(OF STRING)
       CALL 8252   ;(203C hex)
                   ;PRINT STRING
       RET
STRING DEFB 27,64, ;(any codes
            etc.   ; if needed)
       DEFM "MESSAGE"

The same routine will print on
the screen if you LD A,2 at the
start instead. Remember, you
must first initialize the RS232
interface with FORMAT LPRINT "R"
from BASIC.
                  - Brian.

From Neil Morgan, BOLTON

I have been looking into the Clearcut problem on the Spectrum +3[move RAMTOP without a CLS-BC] I agree with you that it should be simple enough. Amstrad supposedly left the 48k ROM pretty well intact but they have made quite a few subtle but major changes to it.

I examined the stacks using the same addresses and similar disassemblers on a 48k machine and on the +3 and found that there were differences in the return addresses for both errors and for correctly executed BASIC lines.

```text
         48k       +3
```

error   1303      5b3a

```text
ok      1b76      1031
```

It would appear a simple change of these values would produce the desired effect.Unfortunately the "ok" value on the +3 sends control to somewhere in the "editing?" area.

I used the Hisoft monitor to alter the error vector and inserted a breakpoint at the new address. The 48k ROM i.e. ROM 3 was in use at the instant that control was returned to the monitor. I have tried the same thing with the "ok" return value but the program never reaches

the breakpoint. On further inspection I found the value on the stack had been reset to it's original value. I suspect that the problem is that a different ROM is in place when a return is made using 1031h but I have been unable to prove this.

Of course it could be that more values on the stack are used on the +3 than used to be used on the 48k, I wish I knew for certain! Perhaps someone can shed some more light on this?

Yes please give us plenty of clip art. I require a picture of a pedal car!Yes I know it sounds silly but it is a real sport with cars costing up to about `1000 (1 thousand, not a

misprint!) which can travel at speeds up to about 40 m.p.h.Many races are 24 hour ones. I need a picture for a newsletter but I am not very artistic.

I'm not sure which issue it is in but Brian Gaff had a routine in popular computing weekly about paging between modes on a +3 which works on some but requires an initial "SPECTRUM" mode change on those with bugged ROMs. I too had difficulty using tape on a +3. The problem was easily solved on my machine with 2 custom made leads. The problem was not with LOADing but the original SAVE. It seemed to save but was actually distorted. A little detective work is needed.

1. Can any commercial program be loaded from cassette at all? If YES then the cassette lead is ok and the head is probably in adjustment. If NO then check the lead is wired correctly bearing in mind that a stereo plug should be used at the Spectrum end.If you still can't load then check the head alignment. 2. If you can load some commercial games but some seem to load then crash, it may be a compatibility problem so:- reset the Spectrum. Go to 48k BASIC FROM THE MENU. LOAD from tape. 3.If all(or most)of the above works then try saving a simple BASIC program to tape. Listen to the tape and if it sounds reasonable try to reload paying close attention to the volume.

4.If 1 and 2 work but 3 fails you will need a specially modified cassette lead or a different cassette recorder. If there is reasonable interest in the custom leads I shall arrange for a batch to be made up.

When a disk is sent through the post it may not always load straight away. Just like video and cassette tapes it should be allowed to reach normal room temperature and humidity before any attempt is made to use it. I tried to load a recent 3" disk version of OUTLET as soon as it arrived and it showed several sector errors. The next day I loaded and transferred all the files without problem.

Any chance of the assembler listing for TANDUM? I have a friend with a Tandy Lineprinter VIII which this code almost works for but the linefeed pitch seems to be wrong. I have the manual but cannot quite work out which bytes to alter to make it work. - Neil Morgan

From: N.J.D. Whittle, CARLUKE

Dear Sirs,

I have been unable to print out any of the OUTLET pages. I use a +3 and a Brother M1509 with its serial socket connected to the RS232 socket on the +3.

Using Toni Baker's book "Master- ing Machine Code on Your Spectrum", I am learning machine code. Printing to the screen is fully described but I would like to incorporate routines to output data to my printer. Can you offer any suggestions?.

To Mr. N.J.D. Whittle from Brian

It has proved impractical to cover all variations of printer interface unfortunately but you can amend it yourself thus...

Select +3 BASIC and enter MERGE "CONTENTS". Wait for the o.k. message. Enter LIST 1356. Wait for the lines to be listed and then press BREAK twice.Press the left-pointing arrow key and the flashing square will move up to the end of line 1300. Press the right arrow key until it moves back down to the space just past the number 1356 at the start of the line. Type a space then: FORMAT LPRINT "R": and ENTER.You will notice the line already has a FORMAT LPRINT "U" which will

be pushed along ahead of your typing. If you get an error BEEP and the flashing square goes red then check your typing. Did you put the colon at the end?

The flashing square should be in the space below line 1356, above 1364. Type RUN 9970 and ENTER which will reSAVE the program to the disc. Re-LOAD OUTLET and try it.I regret that I have not been able to test it as I do not have an RS232 cable but there should be no problem.

The above instruction highlights how awful the 128K editor is to use! If I sounded too pedantic that's for the sake of any other readers who do no programming!

To print from machine code try:

LD A,3      ;stream 3 ;= LPRINT CALL 5633   ;(1601 hex) ;OPEN CHANNEL LD DE,STRING LD BC,LENGTH;(OF STRING) CALL 8252   ;(203C hex) ;PRINT STRING RET STRING DEFB 27,64, ;(any codes etc.   ; if needed) DEFM "MESSAGE"

The same routine will print on the screen if you LD A,2 at the start instead. Remember, you must first initialize the RS232 interface with FORMAT LPRINT "R" from BASIC. - Brian.

### От Neil Morgan, BOLTON

Я исследовал проблему Clearcut на Spectrum +3 [перемещение RAMTOP без выполнения CLS — B.C.]. Я согласен с вами, что это должно быть достаточно просто. Amstrad вроде бы оставил 48k ROM практически нетронутым, но на самом деле они внесли в него довольно много тонких, но существенных изменений.

Я исследовал стеки, используя одни и те же адреса и схожие дизассемблеры на 48k машине и на +3, и обнаружил, что адреса возврата различаются как для ошибок, так и для успешно выполненных строк BASIC:

```text
         48k       +3

error   1303      5b3a
ok      1b76      1031
```

Казалось бы, простое изменение этих значений должно дать нужный эффект. К сожалению, значение «ok» на +3 передаёт управление куда-то в область «редактирования?».

Я использовал монитор Hisoft, чтобы изменить вектор ошибки, и установил точку останова по новому адресу. В момент возврата управления в монитор использовалось ПЗУ 48k, то есть ROM 3. Я попробовал то же самое со значением возврата «ok», но программа так и не достигла точки останова. При дальнейшем исследовании я обнаружил, что значение на стеке было сброшено на исходное. Подозреваю, что загвоздка в том, что при возврате через 1031h подключается другое ПЗУ, но доказать это мне пока не удалось.

Конечно, возможно, что на +3 на стеке используется больше значений, чем раньше на 48k — вот бы знать наверняка! Может быть, кто-нибудь сможет пролить на это свет?

4. Если пункты 1 и 2 работают, а пункт 3 сбоит — вам понадобится специально модифицированный кабель или другой магнитофон. Если к таким заказным кабелям будет достаточный интерес, я организую изготовление партии.

От: N.J.D. Whittle, CARLUKE

Уважаемая редакция,

Я не могу распечатать ни одной страницы из OUTLET. Я использую +3 и принтер Brother M1509, подключённый своим последовательным разъёмом к порту RS232 на +3.

По книге Toni Baker «Mastering Machine Code on Your Spectrum» я изучаю машинный код. Вывод на экран там описан подробно, но мне хотелось бы добавить подпрограммы для вывода данных на принтер. Можете ли вы что-нибудь подсказать?

**Мистеру N.J.D. Whittle от Brian:**

К сожалению, предусмотреть все варианты интерфейсов принтеров на практике оказалось нереально, но вы можете внести исправления самостоятельно следующим образом...

Выберите +3 BASIC и введите `MERGE "CONTENTS"`. Дождитесь сообщения «o.k.». Введите `LIST 1356`. Дождитесь, пока строки выведутся на экран, и затем дважды нажмите BREAK. Нажмите клавишу со стрелкой влево — мигающий курсор переместится в конец строки 1300. Нажимайте стрелку вправо, пока он не опустится обратно в пробел сразу за номером 1356 в начале строки. Напечатайте пробел, затем: `FORMAT LPRINT "R":` и нажмите ENTER. Вы заметите, что в строке уже есть команда `FORMAT LPRINT "U"`, которая просто сдвинется вперёд по мере ввода. Если раздастся сигнал ошибки BEEP, а мигающий квадратик станет красным, проверьте набранное. Не забыли ли вы двоеточие в конце?

Мигающий курсор должен оказаться на пустом месте под строкой 1356, перед 1364. Наберите `RUN 9970` и нажмите ENTER — это заново сохранит программу на диск. Заново загрузите OUTLET через LOAD и попробуйте. К сожалению, я не смог протестировать это лично, так как у меня нет кабеля RS232, но никаких проблем возникнуть не должно.

Эта инструкция наглядно демонстрирует, насколько неудобен редактор 128K! Если я показался излишне педантичным, то лишь ради читателей, которые совсем не занимаются программированием!

Для печати из машинного кода попробуйте:

```text
       LD A,3      ;поток 3
                   ;= LPRINT
       CALL 5633   ;(1601 hex)
                   ;OPEN CHANNEL
       LD DE,STRING
       LD BC,LENGTH;(ДЛИНА СТРОКИ)
       CALL 8252   ;(203C hex)
                   ;PRINT STRING
       RET
STRING DEFB 27,64, ;(любые коды,
            etc.   ; если нужны)
       DEFM "MESSAGE"
```

Та же самая подпрограмма будет выводить текст на экран, если в самом начале вместо этого сделать `LD A,2`. Помните, что сначала необходимо инициализировать интерфейс RS232 командой `FORMAT LPRINT "R"` из BASIC.  
— Brian.
